title: Span stitching for queued handoffs: lightweight continuation token and worker-side stitcher
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: spans are losing causal linkage when requests are handed off to message queues or background workers (e.g., HTTP -> Kafka -> consumer, or job enqueues -> worker pool). This causes broken end-to-end traces and inflated tail latency/errored-span counts in dashboards.

Goal: implement a lightweight, interoperable continuation token and a worker-side 'stitcher' that rehydrates trace context and stitches a child span into the original causal tree without requiring synchronous RPCs or heavy baggage. The solution must be compatible with our Node/Go/Java/Python SDKs and common queue transports (Kafka, SQS, Pub/Sub, Redis streams), minimize per-message overhead, and respect sampling/priority decisions made at the producer.

Scope:
- Define a compact binary token format for message headers (<= 64 bytes typical).
- SDK helpers to attach/extract token across languages and popular client libraries.
- Worker runtime hook that creates a span linked to the original trace and emits a synthetic link/span when the original parent is not present locally.
- Deduplication heuristics for at-least-once delivery scenarios to avoid double-counting.
- Backcompat: if legacy clients don't propagate token, fall back to best-effort local spans and emit a marker event.

Non-goals: full distributed context propagation across arbitrary async libraries (we'll cover major integrations first), trace-level encryption of tokens (deferred to KMS integration), or changing sampling decision semantics mid-flight.
comments: 2025-02-18 Aisha Patel: Created ticket and initial problem statement. Linked to tracing roadmap doc.

2025-02-21 Liam Chen: Spike completed. Implemented PoC in Node consumer that adds 'x-rd-continuation' header (compact base64) and stitches span using created_at/watermark heuristics. PoC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/9404
2025-02-25 Design review (Sofia Martinez): Agreed on token economy (trace_id + parent_id + sampled_flag + origin + 16-bit checksum). Suggested adding a version byte for forward compatibility.

2025-02-27 Eng sync: Decided to keep token client-visible header name 'x-rdinfer-cont' to avoid collisions. Agreed to cap token at 60 bytes and provide a text-fallback header for transports that strip binary headers.

2025-03-01 Liam Chen: Implemented Go SDK extractor and worker stitcher. Added metric 'rd.stitch.success' and 'rd.stitch.duplicate' to help tune dedupe window. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/312
2025-03-04 QA: First integrated smoke tests passing for Kafka and Redis streams. Observed 0.8% increase in message size on average. Still measuring tail latency impact under bursty workloads.
